body:
Ben Carter: quick sync here on deliverability ramp + suppression rules before we flip the switch on onboarding email v2. want to avoid nuking domain rep :grimacing:

Tyler Benson: yep. current plan is a warm/ramp from lifecycle@redwoodinference.com (same sending domain as product updates, but new volume). 

Tyler Benson: proposal:
- Day 1: 10% of eligible cohort (new signups only)
- Day 2: 25%
- Day 3: 50%
- Day 4: 75%
- Day 5: 100%

Tyler Benson: if complaint rate > 0.08% OR hard bounces > 1.5% on any day, we hold at current volume and investigate.

Camila Reyes: +1 on ramp. who’s actually watching the bounce/complaint dashboards daily?

Tyler Benson: I can own. I’m already in SendGrid + Postmaster Tools. I’ll drop a daily note in #marketing and page Ben if we cross thresholds.

Ben Carter: perfect. can you also set up alerts so we don’t rely on humans remembering?

Tyler Benson: yep. I can do:
- SendGrid: event webhook → our internal alerting (basic)
- Gmail Postmaster: manual check (no real-time API), but I can check daily during ramp

Soojin Lee: on suppression — can we be explicit that we suppress anyone who already activated? I don’t want “welcome!” emails hitting folks who already shipped an integration.

Ben Carter: yup. here’s what I have in the send schedule doc, but let’s lock it.

Ben Carter: suppression rules (draft):
1) If `unsubscribe = true` (global) or user opted out of “Product emails” → suppress
2) If user has any of: `first_successful_request` OR `tokens_100k` → suppress onboarding drip entirely
3) If user is in an active Sales opp / enterprise hand-raise segment → suppress (avoid mixed motion)
4) If support flag indicates “do not contact” / bounces previously → suppress

Michael Grant: adding: make sure we’re honoring unsubscribe across ALL lifecycle sends (CAN-SPAM/GDPR). also, “product emails” vs “onboarding tips” category needs to be consistent in the preference center language.

Tyler Benson: re #2 — careful: we may still want a single “here’s where to find usage dashboard / rate limits” email even after first request. but if we’re being conservative for deliverability, suppressing is safest.

Ben Carter: for this sprint, I’d rather be conservative. we can add “post-activation” later.

Leila Farouk: QA note: suppression based on activation events depends on event timeliness. if there’s lag in token metering, someone could activate and still get email 2.

Tyler Benson: good call. we can implement a “cooldown” check at send time:
- if last_seen_request_ts within 24h, suppress today’s send

Ben Carter: love that. also, can we add a “don’t send within first 15 min after signup” rule? reduces accidental sends to folks who bounce immediately / typo emails.

Tyler Benson: yes. debounce window is easy.

Camila Reyes: what metrics are we using as stop/go again?

Tyler Benson: deliverability guardrails during ramp:
- Hard bounce rate: target < 1.0%, hold if > 1.5%
- Spam complaint rate: target < 0.05%, hold if > 0.08%
- Unsubscribe rate: not a hard stop, but investigate if > 1.0% (usually copy/targeting issue)
- Deferred/dropped: watch spikes (could be throttling)

Soojin Lee: copy side: if unsub spikes, I can tweak subject line aggressiveness + remove “benchmarks” language from the opener. but ideally we fix targeting first.

Ben Carter: Tyler — can you post the “owner + escalation path” so we’re clear?

Tyler Benson: sure:
Owner (daily monitoring during ramp): Tyler
Backup: Ben
Escalation:
- deliverability issue (bounces/complaints): Tyler → #marketing + DM Ben + file INT ticket (INT-3301 if auth/DKIM/SPF/DMARC)
- user reports “not receiving emails”: route to Support (SUP queue) + Tyler checks suppression / provider logs

Michael Grant: and if we change preference center language or categories, loop me in before it goes live.

Ben Carter: :thumbsup: last question: do we exclude internal + test accounts?

Tyler Benson: yes — suppression list includes:
- @redwoodinference.com, @redwood.ai
- our seed/test domains list
- anyone tagged “qa_test” in user profile

Leila Farouk: can you add my QA aliases too? I don’t want to pollute complaint rate if I’m hammering the flow.

Tyler Benson: yep, DM me the list.

Camila Reyes: looks good. please keep the ramp conservative, even if it slows experiment velocity. rather have clean infra for the rest of the quarter.

Ben Carter: agreed. locking this. Tyler, once you add alerts + debounce/cooldown checks, ping here and I’ll update the sprint brief.

Tyler Benson: will do. (also confirming DKIM/SPF are green on current sender domain — but I’ll re-verify before Day 1)

Ben Carter: thanks all. :shipit:
